subject: A doubt in the Impute argument in itemfit function

messages.author: 84aac2580b195c68
messages.subject: A doubt in the Impute argument in itemfit function
parts:
Dear Phil,

I was using itemfit to calculate fit of the items for the missing data. I observed that there is some standard deviation also getting calculated for the corresponding fit indices. When I tried to debug the itemfit, I did not find any random factor which would change the values of ave and SD (the data.frame  which you have used to calculate the average estimate and the standard deviation of them.

In the list collect where you are storing the all the values for each iteration of imputation, I saw that in all iterations, the values of the fit indices were not changing.
However my SD was coming 0. If nothing is not changing all SDs must be zero. There must be something varying which I am not able to see.

Please help


Regards,
Irshad

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: A doubt in the Impute argument in itemfit function
parts:
I'm still a little confused by what you mean. The data are imputed given the latent trait value and item parameters to form the probability of selecting a particular category, and the selected category is then randomly sampled given the probability weights. So, individuals with very high latent traits will more likely have imputed values of 1, since the sampling categories will be weighted like sample(c(0,1), 1, prob = c(.01, .99)) --- or whatever the expected values end up being (see ?probtrace to check what the weights are yourself). Low traits will be the opposite. Does that make sense?

Phil
